CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male with type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux who presents with complaints of shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. Patient reports noticing swelling in his legs and attributes symptoms to dietary indiscretion, specifically consuming salty foods at house parties. He describes feeling lethargic. Dyspnea occurs with exertion, particularly when walking up stairs. He also reports some discomfort when lying flat in bed and stiffness upon waking in the morning. Patient experienced one episode of acute nocturnal dyspnea approximately one week ago but has not had recurrence. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorsed shortness of breath. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, and abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 1 diabetes mellitus
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Gastroesophageal reflux disease

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump
Omeprazole 20 milligrams daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports maintaining good blood sugar monitoring during the work week but occasionally misses monitoring on weekends. Admits to consuming chocolate bars regularly. Has attempted natural solutions for depression including outdoor stretches during summer months. Has reduced red bull and caffeine intake. Alcohol intake has been difficult during holiday season but improving.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Within normal limits. Pulse oximetry: normal.
Neck: No jugular venous distension appreciated. No carotid bruits.
Heart: 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated.
Lungs: Crackles appreciated bilaterally at the bases.
Lower extremities: 1+ pitting edema noted.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease.
Laboratory studies: White blood cell count not elevated. No evidence of infection or pneumonia.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute heart failure exacerbation: Initiate lasix 40 milligrams daily. Patient instructed to weigh himself daily and call if weight does not decrease or if weight increases. Patient instructed to seek emergency care if shortness of breath worsens at rest.

2. Type 1 diabetes mellitus: Order hemoglobin A1c to be checked in approximately one month to assess for need for medication adjustments. Recommend follow-up with endocrinologist. Ensure patient has recent eye exam.

3. Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications at this time. Patient open to suggestions.

4. Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Continue omeprazole 20 milligrams daily.
